# Release notes: a reported bike leaves service at once

## Riders

- When you report a broken bike in the app, we take it out of service right away.
- No one else can rent that bike while it waits for repair.
- The station map now shows how many bikes are ready to ride and how many are broken at each station.
- You may see a few more broken bikes on the map. That means the map is telling the truth.
- Thank you for reporting broken bikes. Every report helps keep the next rider safe.

## Crews

- The queue now puts the job that is due first on top. Ties go to the earlier report, then the job id.
- The 48 hour clock for a rider report starts when the rider reports the bike, not when the job is opened.
- Defects a crew finds itself still get 96 hours, counted from when the crew found them.
- Jobs already open move to the same rule: their due times come up to 1 hour earlier. None is overdue because of this.
- A rider report now takes the bike out of service at once. There is no way yet to put it back in the app, so a fixed bike stays out until a follow-up change adds one.

# Rollout plan: a reported bike leaves service at once (P-2 to P-5).
# Thresholds come only from data/contract/sla.yaml. Districts come from data/stations.csv.

# No flag exists in src/ yet. This is the proposed name; the change must be put behind it before stage 1.
feature_flag: wrench_disables_bike

stages:
  - districts: [North]    # 40 stations
  - districts: [East]     # 30 stations
  - districts: [Centre]   # 40 stations
  - districts: [South, West]   # 35 + 35 stations

guardrails:
  - metric: rentable_fleet_percent        # share of bikes riders can rent, checked in every district
    stop_below: 96                        # SLA-9 minimum_percent
  - metric: repairs_on_time_percent       # repair jobs fixed within the SLA-4 limits (48h wrench, 96h crew-found)
    stop_below: 95                        # SLA-4 target_percent
  - metric: wrench_job_age_hours          # oldest open job from a rider wrench, counted from the wrench
    stop_above: 48                        # SLA-4 wrenched_limit_hours
  - metric: crew_found_job_age_hours      # oldest open job a crew found itself
    stop_above: 96                        # SLA-4 not_wrenched_limit_hours
  - metric: station_outage_hours          # longest current outage at any single station
    stop_above: 4                         # SLA-11 limit_hours
  - metric: feed_age_seconds              # age of the data in the public GBFS feed
    stop_above: 60                        # SLA-12 feed_max_age_seconds

rollback:
  command: bun run rollback   # needs a person to say yes first (AGENTS.md)
  when: >-
    Any guardrail above crosses its threshold in a district that is in the rollout,
    and turning feature_flag off for that district does not bring it back within the stage.

content.text:
I wrote `work/rollout.yaml`. I couldn't check that it parses, because the command to load it with Bun needed approval.

**One problem first:** there is no feature flag in the code. Nothing in `src/` or `work/` defines one. I used the name `wrench_disables_bike` and marked it in a comment as a proposal. Someone has to put the change behind that flag before stage 1, or the plan has nothing to switch on and off per district.

What the file contains:

- **Stages:** North (40 stations), then East (30), then Centre (40), then South and West together (35 + 35). These are the five districts in `data/stations.csv`, in the order the file lists them. I grouped the last two because they are the smallest. You can split them if you'd rather keep one district per stage.
- **Guardrails:** each threshold is taken directly from `sla.yaml`, with a comment naming its SLA id:
  - **SLA-9:** stop if the share of rentable bikes falls below 96%, checked in each district.
  - **SLA-4:** stop if repairs done on time fall below 95%.
  - **SLA-4:** stop if an open rider-report job is older than 48 hours.
  - **SLA-4:** stop if an open crew-found job is older than 96 hours.
  - **SLA-11:** stop if any one station has been out for more than 4 hours.
  - **SLA-12:** stop if the public feed's data is more than 60 seconds old.
- **Rollback:** the command is `bun run rollback`, which is in `package.json`. You run it when a guardrail is crossed in a district that has the change and turning the flag off there doesn't fix it within the stage. The file notes that a person must approve the rollback first, as AGENTS.md requires.

**The SLA-9 guardrail may stop the rollout on its own.** With this release, reported bikes show as out of service at once, so the rentable share will honestly go down. If a district is already close to 96%, it could cross the line just from more accurate counts. Someone should check each district's current rentable share before starting North.
